farraa:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَمَنَّوْاْ مَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾ — this is not a prohibition that makes something forbidden; it is only a lesson in good conduct (adab) from Allah. It came about because Umm Salama and others said: "Would that we were men, so that we could fight in jihad and go on campaigns and have a reward like the reward of men." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down ﴿وَلاَ تَتَمَنَّوْاْ مَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ﴾. And it has been reported: "Let none of you wish for his brother's wealth; rather let him say: O Allah, provide for me; O Allah, give to me."

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱلصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ — in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is (فالصوالح قوانت). Both the pattern fawāʿil and the pattern fāʿilāt are acceptable as the plural of fāʿila.
His saying: ﴿بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ — the reading is with the nominative (rafʿ). Its meaning is: guarding the absence of their husbands because Allah guarded them, when He enjoined the husbands concerning them. Some read it (بما حـَفظ اللَّه) with the accusative, making the verb act upon an object (wāqiʿ), as though you said: guarding the unseen by that which keeps Allah [i.e. His rights]; just as you say: "by what pleases Allah", making the verb belong to «ما», so that it takes on the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun). I do not favour it, because it is not a verb with a known agent; it is rather like a maṣdar.
His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَبْغُواْ عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلاً﴾ — He is saying: do not seek pretexts against them.
His saying: ﴿وَٱللاَّتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ﴾ — the exegesis has come that the meaning of «تخافون» is "you know".
It is like ẓann (supposition), because the one who supposes is like the one who doubts, and the one who fears may also hope. That is why "fear" came to resemble "supposing" and "knowing". Do you not see that you say of a piece of news that reaches you: "By Allah, I feared that," and you say: "I supposed that," and the meaning of the two is the same? That is why the poet said:
ولا تدفِنَنِّى بالفَلاة فإننى * أخاف إذا ما مُِتُّ أنْ لا أذوقها
(Do not bury me in the open desert, for I fear [i.e. I think] that when I die I shall not taste it [the wine].)
And another said:
أتانى كلام عن نُصَيْب يقوله * وما خفت يا سلاّم أنك عائبى
(Words reached me that Nuṣayb was saying, and I did not fear [i.e. think], O Sallām, that you would find fault with me.)
It is as though he said: "and I did not suppose that you would find fault with me." And we have transmitted in the hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was commanded to use the tooth-stick (siwāk) until I feared that I would lose my teeth" — like your saying: "until I supposed that I would lose my teeth."

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱبْعَثُواْ حَكَماً مِّنْ أَهْلِهِ وَحَكَماً مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ﴾ — He is saying: an arbiter from the man's family and an arbiter from the woman's family, so that they may learn from which of the two the discord (nushūz) came.
The arbiter should go to the man and wait to see what he has in mind: does he love the woman? If he says, "No, by Allah, I have no need of her," he knows that the discord came from his side. The woman's arbiter says the same sort of thing to her. Then the two of them inform both spouses according to that, and they go to the husband and say: "You are a wrongdoer, you are a wrongdoer; fear Allah!" — if he is the wrongdoer. That is His saying ﴿إِن يُرِيدَآ إِصْلاَحاً يُوَفِّقِ ٱللَّهُ بَيْنَهُمَآ﴾, i.e. if the two of them do this.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱعْبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلاَ تُشْرِكُواْ بِهِ شَيْئاً وَبِٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً﴾ — He commanded them to do good to the parents. Similar to it is ﴿وقضى ربُّك ألاّ تَعْبُدوا إلا إيّاه وبالوالدين إحسانا﴾. Had «الإحسان» been put in the nominative by means of the bā' [i.e. as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the prepositional phrase as its khabar (predicate)], since the verb is not expressed, it would have been correct; just as you say in ordinary speech: "Do good to your brother, and to the evil-doer evil" [with «الإساءة» nominative].
﴿وَٱلْجَارِ ذِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾ is in the genitive. In some of the codices of the people of Kufa and the old codices it is written (ذا القربى) with alif. Whoever reads it with the alif should put it in the accusative, (والجارَ ذا القربى), so that it is like His saying ﴿حافظوا على الصلواتِ والصلاَة الوسطى﴾ [as read with the accusative], implying a verb by which the accusative comes about.
﴿وَٱلْجَارِ ٱلْجُنُبِ﴾: the neighbour between whom and you there is no kinship; ﴿وَٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلجَنْبِ﴾: the travelling companion; ﴿وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾: the guest.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿ فَسَآءَ قِرِيناً﴾ is equivalent to your saying "What an excellent man!" (niʿma rajulan) and "What a wretched man!" (biʾsa rajulan). Likewise ﴿وساءت مصيرا﴾ and ﴿كَبُر مقتا﴾. The construction of niʿma and biʾsa and the like is that they put in the accusative the indefinite nouns that follow them, and put in the nominative the definite noun that follows them when it is not specific [i.e. a generic definite with al-], together with whatever is annexed to such a definite noun. What is annexed to an indefinite noun may take either the nominative or the accusative.
If the discourse has gone forward with a masculine noun whose khabar (predicate) has been made feminine, as in "The abode (al-dār, fem.) is a dwelling (manzil, masc.) of truth," you say: niʿmat manzilan [with the feminine verb], just as He said ﴿وساءت مصيرا﴾ and said ﴿حسنت مرتفقا﴾. Had it been said "wa-sāʾa maṣīran" and "wa-ḥasuna murtafaqan", it would have been correct, just as you say: biʾsa al-manzilu al-nāru, and niʿma al-manzilu al-jannatu. Masculine and feminine follow this principle. It is also permissible to say: niʿmat al-manzilu dāruka, making the verb of «المنزل» feminine because it is a description of the abode (dār). Likewise you say: niʿma al-dāru manziluka, making the verb of «الدار» masculine since it is a description of the dwelling. Dhū al-Rumma said:
أو حُرَّةٌ عَيْطَل ثبْجاءُ مُجْفِرةٌ * دعائمَ الزَّورِ نِعمت زورقُ البلد
(Or a noble, long-necked, broad-backed she-camel, wide in the supports of the chest — what an excellent boat of the desert she is!)
It is permissible to mention two men and say biʾsā rajulayni and biʾsa rajulayni, and for a group: niʿma qawman and niʿmū qawman. The same goes for the feminine plural. They kept the verb singular even though it came after nouns [referring to more than one] only because biʾsa and niʿma are an indication of praise or blame, and they were not meant in the way of an [ordinary] verb such as qāmā and qaʿadā ("the two stood", "the two sat"). This is regular and frequent with biʾsa and niʿma, and it is sometimes said with other verbs that carry the meaning of biʾsa and niʿma.
One of the Arabs said: "I composed verses — how excellent they were as verses! (jāda abyātan)," keeping the verb for the verses singular. Al-Kisāʾī used to say: [the meaning is] implied, "jāda bihinna abyātan"; but there is nothing implied here: it is only the verb and what is contained in it. [Translator's note: the text here reads «حاد بهن», evidently a misprint for «جاد بهن».]
His saying: ﴿وحَسُنَ أولئك رفيقا﴾ — He made «الرفيق» singular although it describes a plural only because the Arabs use rafīq (companion), barīd (courier) and rasūl (messenger) both for one and for many. That is why He said ﴿وحَسُن أولئِك رفيقا﴾. In ordinary speech of this kind it is not permissible to say "ḥasuna ulāʾika rajulan" or "qabuḥa ulāʾika rajulan"; it is only permissible to make the description of a plural singular when it is a noun derived from a verb and not a plain noun such as rajul (man) and imraʾa (woman). Do you not see that the poet said:
وإذا هُمُ طعِموا فألأم طاعم * وإذا هم جاعوا فشرّ جِياع
(When they eat, they are the meanest of eaters [singular]; and when they hunger, they are the worst of hungry ones [plural].)
And His saying: ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلمةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِم﴾ is likewise. Some put it in the nominative and did not place an implied pronoun before it from which «الكلمة» would come out [as tamyīz (specification)]. If you put it in the accusative, it comes out of His saying ﴿ويُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَداً﴾, i.e. "this has become great as a word."

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضَاعِفْهَا﴾ — «الحسنة» is put in the accusative and a nominative noun is implied in (تك) [as its subject]. If you wish, you can put «الحسنة» in the nominative and imply nothing. It is like His saying ﴿وإن كانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ فَنَظرَة إلى مَيْسرة﴾.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَعَصَوُاْ ٱلرَّسُولَ لَوْ تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ ٱلأَرْضُ﴾ — [also read] (وتسوى). Its meaning is: would that they were levelled with the dust. They wished that only because on the Day of Resurrection the wild beasts and all the other animals will be told: "Be dust!" Then the people of Paradise are brought to life. When the unbelievers see that, they say to one another: "Come, let us say, when we are questioned: 'By Allah, we were not polytheists.'" When they are questioned and say it, their mouths are sealed and their limbs are given leave [to speak], and they bear witness against them. Then they wish that they had been dust and had not concealed any statement from Allah. So "concealing the statement" here falls within what they wish for.
It is also said: the meaning is only: "On that day they will not conceal from Allah any statement, and they will wish that the earth were levelled with them."

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَقْرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ﴾ — it was revealed concerning a group of the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ who drank and then attended the prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before wine was forbidden. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down ﴿لاَ تَقْرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ﴾ with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but pray it in your dwellings.
Then He said ﴿وَلاَ جُنُباًً﴾, i.e. do not approach it in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَغْتَسِلُواْ﴾. Then He made an exception and said ﴿إِلاَّ عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ﴾ — He is saying: unless you are travellers who are unable to find water. Then He said ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُواْ﴾. Tayammum is to make for clean earth wherever it may be. Tayammum is nothing but one strike for the face and one strike for the hands, for the person in a state of major impurity and for others alike. [Translator's note: the text reads «الصعد», evidently for «الصعيد» (earth).]

farraa:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ﴾ — ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ throughout the Qurʾān means: "Have you not been told?" In Arabic it can also mean: "Do you not see?", "Do you not know?"

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ﴾ — if you wish, you can make it connected to His saying ﴿ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصِيبا من الكتاب﴾ … ﴿مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ﴾; and if you wish, it is cut off from it and resumptive (mustaʾnaf), the meaning being: "Among those who are Jews are some who distort the words." This is part of the speech of the Arabs: they imply «من» ("some who") at the beginning of an utterance, and say: "Of us [some] say that, and of us [some] do not say it." That is because «مِن» denotes a part of that of which it is [a part], and so it conveys the meaning that has been left out. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿وما مِنّا إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقامٌ مَعْلُوم﴾ and said ﴿وإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلا وارِدها﴾. And Dhū al-Rumma said:
فظلّوا ومنهم دمعه سابِقٌ له * وآخرُ يثْنِى دَمْعَة العين بالْهَمْلِ
(They remained, and of them [was one] whose tears outran him, and another who held back the tear of the eye from flowing.)
He means: of them was one whose tears outran him. Implying «من» is not permissible with any of the prepositions (ṣifāt) except in the sense I have told you of. A poet has said it with «فى», but I do not favour it; he said:
لو قلت ما فى قومها لم تأْثم * يَفْضُلها فى حسب ومِيسم
(Were you to say, "There is none among her people who surpasses her in noble lineage and beauty," you would not sin.)
It is also transmitted as (تيثم), a dialectal form. That was permissible with «فى» only because you find in it the meaning of «من», namely that it is part of what it is attached to. Do you not see that you say: "Among us (fīnā) are righteous people and among us are those below that," as though you had said "of us (minnā)"? But it is not permissible to say "In the house says that," meaning "In the house is someone who says that"; it is only permissible when you attach «فى» to the genus of what has been left out.
His saying: ﴿لَيّاً بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ﴾ — He means: they say (وراعِنا), turning it into an insult against Muhammad ﷺ. That is the "twisting" (layy).
His saying: ﴿وَأَقْوَمَ﴾ — i.e. more just.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾ — if you wish, you can treat it [«أن يشرك»] as being in the genitive, then drop the preposition so that it becomes accusative; it then carries a conditional sense (jazāʾ), as though you said: "Allah does not forgive a sin together with shirk, nor [a sin] arising from shirk."

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ — the Jews brought their children to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Do these have any sins?" He said: "No." They said: "Then we are like them: whatever we do by night is expiated for us by day, and whatever we do by day is expiated for us by night." That is their declaring themselves pure.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلاً﴾ — the fatīl is the dirt that you roll between your two fingers; it is also said that it is the [thread] in the cleft of the date-stone.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ فَإِذاً لاَّ يُؤْتُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ نَقِيراً﴾ — the naqīr is the speck on the back of the date-stone. As for (إذاً): when an utterance is begun with it, it puts in the accusative the verb that begins with yāʾ, tāʾ, nūn or alif [i.e. the imperfect verb]; one says: "idhan aḍribaka" ("then I will strike you"), "idhan ajziyaka" ("then I will repay you"). If it has with it fāʾ, wāw, thumma or «أو» — one of the conjunctions — then, if you wish, the two together carry the sense of a fresh beginning and you also put [the verb] in the accusative with it; and if you wish, you treat the fāʾ or the wāw, when they are attached to it, as being transferred from it to something else. The meaning of His saying ﴿فَإِذاً لاَّ يُؤْتُونَ﴾ is: "then they would not give people a speck, in that case (idhan)." What shows you this is that in meaning — and Allah knows best — it is the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied conditional, as though you said: "And if they had — or: and were they to have — a share, they would not, in that case, give people a speck." In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is in the accusative: (فإذا لا يؤتوا الناس نقيرا).
If you see that the utterance is complete, as in your saying "Are you standing?", and then you say "fa-idhan aḍribaka", you put it in the accusative by idhan, [or] you put it in the accusative as the answer of the fāʾ, and intend the transfer. Likewise with commands and prohibitions, two ways are valid with idhan: the accusative by it, and transferring it. If you wish, you can put the verb in the nominative when you intend the transfer, and say: "Come to him, fa-idhan yukrimuka," meaning "for he will honour you, in that case," without making it the answer.
When a conditional precedes it and it is the apodosis to it, you say: "In taʾtinī idhan ukrimuka" ("If you come to me, then I will honour you"); and if you wish: "idhan ukrimaka" and "ukrimka". Whoever uses the jussive means "ukrimka idhan"; whoever uses the accusative intends in idhan a fāʾ that is the answer, and puts the verb in the accusative by idhan; and whoever uses the nominative treats idhan as transferred to the end of the utterance, as though he said: "fa-ukrimuka idhan."
When you see a lām in the apodosis of idhan, then «لئن», an oath, or «لو» has been implied for it. Of this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ما اتّخذ اللَّهُ من ولدٍ وما كان مَعَه مِن إِلهٍ إِذاً لذهب كُلُّ إِلهٍ بِما خلق﴾. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Had there been [with Him] in them a god, each god would have taken away what it had created." Similar is ﴿وإِن كادوا لَيَفْتنونك عنِ الذِى أَوحينا إِليك لِتفترِىَ علينا غيرَه، وإذا لاتّخَذوك خلِيلا﴾, whose meaning is: "had you done so, they would have taken you [as a friend]." Likewise His saying ﴿كِدْتَ تركن﴾ and then He said ﴿إِذاً لأذقناك﴾ — its meaning is: "had you inclined, We would then have made you taste."
When you apply (إذاً) to a yafʿalu-verb and a noun precedes it, it becomes void and does not cause the accusative; so you say: "anā idhan aḍribuka." When «إنّ» stands at the beginning of the utterance, you may put the verb in the accusative or the nominative; you say: "innī idhan ūdhiyaka." The nominative is permissible. One of the Arabs recited to me:
لا تتركنِّى فِيهُم شَطيرا * إِنى إِذاً أهلِكَ أو أَطيرا
(Do not leave me among them a stranger, for then I would perish or fly away.)

farraa:54-55.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَىٰ مَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ — these are the Jews, who envied the Prophet ﷺ his many wives and said: "This man claims that he is a prophet, yet he has no concern except women."
So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down ﴿فَقَدْ آتَيْنَآ آلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلْكِتَابَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ﴾ — and among the family of Abraham was Solomon son of David, who had nine hundred wives, and David had a hundred wives.
When this verse was recited to them, some of them disbelieved and some believed.
That is His saying: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ آمَنَ بِهِ﴾, i.e. in the report about Solomon and David, ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن صَدَّ عَنْهُ﴾ by denial and turning away.

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ خُذُواْ حِذْرَكُمْ فَٱنفِرُواْ ثُبَاتٍ أَوِ ٱنْفِرُواْ جَمِيعاً﴾ — He is saying: in bands, when you are called to the raiding parties; or [go forth all together] when you are called to go forth all together.

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ﴾ — the lām on (من) came in because of the presence of «إنّ», just as you say: "inna fīhā la-akhāka" ("indeed in it is your brother").
The lām entered (لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ), which is the ṣila (relative clause) of «من», by the implication of something resembling an oath; just as you say in speech: "This is the one who will surely stand (la-yaqūmanna)," and "I see a man who will surely do (la-yafʿalanna) what he wants." The lām enters more easily into indefinite nouns that have a relative clause than into «من», «ما» and «الذى», because one cannot stop on them [i.e. they cannot stand without their ṣila].
The rule for "a man" (al-rajul) and «الذى» is one and the same when they need a ṣila. His saying ﴿وإنّ كُلاّ لما لَيُوَفِّينّهم﴾ is of this kind: the lām entered «ما» because of «إنّ», and entered the ṣila just as it entered «ليبطئن». This is not permissible with ʿAbd Allāh and Zayd [i.e. proper names]: you may not say "inna akhāka la-yaqūmanna", because "brother" and Zayd do not need a ṣila, and the lām is not fit to enter their khabar (predicate) when it comes later; for when an oath falls between the noun and its khabar, its answer becomes void. Thus we say: "Zaydun wa-llāhi yukrimuka" ("Zayd — by Allah — honours you"), and you do not say "Zaydun wa-llāhi la-yukrimuka."

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿يٰلَيتَنِي كُنتُ مَعَهُمْ فَأَفُوزَ فَوْزاً عَظِيماً﴾ — the Arabs put in the accusative what they answer with the fāʾ after «ليت», because it expresses a wish, and in a wish there is the sense of "it would please me that you do, and then I would do." This is an accusative as though it were conjoined (mansūq), as in your saying in speech: "I wished that I might stand and then people would follow me (fa-yattabiʿanī)." And it is a sound answer to a negation (jaḥd) that is intended in the wish, because what is wished for, among things already past, is as though negated. Do you not see that in His saying ﴿يٰلَيتَنِي كُنتُ مَعَهُمْ فَأَفُوزَ﴾ the meaning is: "[were] I with them, I would triumph"? And His saying in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām ﴿يا ليتنا نُرَدُّ ولا نُكَذِّبَ﴾ is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh with the fāʾ: ﴿نردّ فلا نكذبَ بآياتِ ربّنا﴾. Whoever reads it that way may use the accusative as the answer, or the nominative as a fresh beginning, i.e. "and then we will not deny." In our reading it is with the wāw; so in our reading the nominative is better than the accusative, and the accusative is permissible by way of ṣarf [the wāw of concomitance that turns the verb away from conjunction], as in your saying: "Nothing is too wide for me and then too narrow for you (wa-yaḍīqa ʿanka)."

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ لاَ تُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾ — (المستضعفين) is in the position of the genitive.
His saying: ﴿ٱلظَّالِمِ أَهْلُهَا﴾ — (الظالم) is in the genitive because it is a naʿt (adjective) for «أهل» [grammatically for «القرية»]: when He referred «الأهل» back to the town, the action of what is annexed to it was treated as the action of the town itself; just as you say: "I passed by the man whose house is spacious (al-wāsiʿati dāruhu)," and as you say: "I passed by a man whose eye is beautiful (ḥasanatin ʿaynuhu)." In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "أخرجنا من القرية التي كانت ظالمة". Similar to it — where wrongdoing is ascribed to the town while the wrongdoing actually belongs to its people — occurs in more than one place in the Revelation; of that is ﴿وكَمْ مِن قَرْيةٍ أهلكناها﴾, and of it is His saying ﴿واسألِ القرية التِى كنا فِيها﴾, which means: ask the people of the town. [Translator's note: the text reads «القربة», evidently a misprint for «القرية».]

farraa:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي بُرُوجٍ مُّشَيَّدَةٍ﴾ — the doubled form is used for what is a plural, as in your saying: "I passed by dyed garments (muṣabbagha) and slaughtered rams (mudhabbaḥa)."
The doubling (tashdīd) is permissible because the action is spread over a plurality. If you take one single item of that, then, if the action is repeated and multiplied in the single item, both the doubled and the undoubled forms are permissible, as in your saying: "I passed by a man covered with head wounds (mushajjaj), and by a torn garment (mumazzaq)"; the doubling is permissible because the action has been repeated and multiplied in it.
And you say: "I passed by a slaughtered (madhbūḥ) ram," and do not say "mudhabbaḥ", because slaughtering is not repeated as tearing is repeated. His saying ﴿وبِئرٍ مُعَطَّلةٍ وقصرٍ مَشِيد﴾ — the doubled form is permissible in it, because tashyīd is building, and so it is drawn out and repeated. Whatever else occurs is measured by analogy with this.
His saying: ﴿وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ حَسَنَةٌ يَقُولُواْ هَـٰذِهِ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَقُولُواْ هَـٰذِهِ مِنْ عِندِكَ﴾ — that is because when the Prophet ﷺ came to the Jews in Medina, they said: "We have never seen a man of worse omen than this one: our fruits have decreased and our prices have risen." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: if they receive rain and abundance they say, "This is from Allah," and if their prices rise they say, "This is on account of Muhammad ﷺ."
And the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿قُلْ كُلٌّ مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
His saying: ﴿فَمَالِ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ ٱلْقَوْمِ﴾ — (فمال) became so frequent in speech that they imagined the lām to be joined to «ما», as if it were one of its letters. Because of the continuity of the reading, it is not permissible to stop on the lām, since it is a lām that governs the genitive.

farraa:81-81.t:
His saying: ﴿طَاعَةٌ﴾ — the nominative is according to your saying: "From us [there is] obedience," or "Your command is [one of] obedience." Likewise ﴿قُل لاَ تُقْسِمُوا طَاعَةٌ مَّعْرُوفَةٌ﴾, which means — and Allah knows best —: "Say: hearing and obedience." Likewise the one in the sūra of Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿فأَولى لهم طاعةٌ وقولٌ معروف﴾: it is not put in the nominative by (لهم); it is in the nominative in the way I have mentioned to you. That is because the command to fight was sent down to them and they said, "Hearing and obedience," but when they left Muhammad ﷺ they changed what they had said. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿فلو صدقوا الله لكان خيرا لهم﴾. Some grammarians say: "and fighting was mentioned in it, and (طاعة) was mentioned" — but there is no wāw in it, so that this interpretation could be permissible. If you referred «الطاعة» back and made it as if it were an explanation of «القتال», both the nominative and the accusative would be permissible: the accusative meaning "fighting was mentioned in it with obedience" or "upon obedience"; and the nominative meaning "fighting was mentioned in it; obedience was mentioned in it."
His saying: ﴿بَيَّتَ طَآئِفَةٌ﴾ — the reading is with the tāʾ in the accusative [i.e. with fatḥa], because it is in the pattern faʿala [a past verb].
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "بيّتَ مُبيّت منهم" غير الذى تقول ("one of them plotted by night other than what you say"). Its meaning: they changed what they had said and acted contrary to it. Ḥamza read it with the jussive [i.e. sukūn] and read it «بيَّتْ طائفة»; he gave it sukūn because of the many vowels, and when the tāʾ became vowelless it was assimilated into the ṭāʾ.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا جَآءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَمْنِ أَوِ ٱلْخَوْفِ﴾ — this was revealed concerning the raiding parties that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to send out. Whenever they were victorious or defeated, the hypocrites hastened to seek news of the state of the raiding parties, and then spread it before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made it public or spoken of it. So He said ﴿أَذَاعُواْ بِهِ﴾ — He is saying: they spread it. Had they not done so, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the one to tell of it, it would have been better for them — or had they referred it to the commanders of the raiding parties. That is His saying ﴿وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ وَإِلَىٰ أُوْلِي ٱلأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ لَعَلِمَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنْهُمْ﴾. And His saying: ﴿لاَتَّبَعْتُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾ — the exegetes said its meaning is: "those who investigate it would have known it, except a few." It is also said: "they spread it, except a few." This is the better of the two interpretations, because when news of the raiding parties becomes public, both the investigator and others know it, whereas spreading may happen with some of them and not others. That is why I consider the exception from the spreading to be better.

farraa:85-85.t:
His saying: ﴿ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كِفْلٌ مِّنْهَا﴾ — the kifl is the portion. From it is His saying ﴿يؤتِكم كِفْلَيْنِ مِن رحمتِهِ﴾, meaning: two portions.
His saying: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُّقِيتاً﴾ — al-muqīt is the one who determines and has power over things, like one who gives every man his sustenance (qūt). It has come in the hadith: "It is enough [sin] for a man that he neglects those whom he sustains (yuqīt)" — also "yaqūt".

farraa:86-86.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّواْ بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَآ﴾} — i.e. add to it; as when someone says "Peace be upon you," and the other says "And upon you, and the mercy of Allah." This is the addition. ﴿أَوْ رُدُّوهَآ﴾ — this was said for the Muslims. As for the People of the Book, nothing is added for them beyond "And upon you."

farraa:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَا لَكُمْ فِي ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ﴾ — they had been speaking about some people who emigrated from Mecca to Medina, then grew weary of it and found its climate unhealthy, and so returned secretly to Mecca. Some of the Muslims said: "If we meet them, we will kill them and take their spoils." And some of the Muslims said: "Will you kill people who follow your religion because they found Medina unhealthy?" Allah made them hypocrites, and Allah said: "Why are you divided concerning the hypocrites?" That is His saying (فئتين).
Then He said, confirming their hypocrisy, ﴿وَدُّوا لو تَكْفُرون كما كَفَروا﴾. He put (فئتين) in the accusative by the verb [implied in «ما لكم»]; you say "Mā laka qāʾiman?" ("Why are you standing?"), just as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿فَمَا لِلّذِينَ كَفَروا قِبلك مُهْطِعِين﴾. It does not matter whether the accusative word is definite or indefinite; in speech it is permissible to say "Mā laka al-nāẓira fī amrinā?" ("Why are you the one looking into our affair?"), because it is like the verb that makes the accusative, such as kāna, aẓunnu and the like.
In every place where faʿala and yafʿalu are fit [to stand] for the accusative word, both the definite and the indefinite may be put in the accusative, just as kāna and aẓunnu make the accusative; for they are deficient (nawāqiṣ) in meaning, even if you think they are complete.
Like «مالِ» are "Mā bāluka?" and "Mā shaʾnuka?" Operating these expressions in the way I have told you is easy and common. But do not say "Mā amruka al-qāʾima?" or "Mā khaṭbuka al-qāʾima?" by analogy with them; for they [the former] have become frequent, and what has not been used is not measured by analogy with what has been used. Do you not see that they said "Ayshin ʿindaka?" ("What do you have?"), yet analogy on this is not permissible in any other expression?
His saying: ﴿والله أَرْكَسَهُمْ بما كَسبوا﴾ — He is saying: He turned them back to unbelief. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy it is ﴿واللَّه رَكَسَهم﴾.

farraa:100-100.t: His saying: ﴿يَجِدْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مُرَاغَماً كَثِيراً﴾ — [murāgham] and murāghama are two maṣdars (verbal nouns). Al-murāgham is a place to move about and a way to go in the land.

farraa:102-102.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلْتَقُمْ﴾ — every lām of command, when it begins the utterance and has no wāw, fāʾ or thumma before it, takes kasra. When one of these particles is with it, it takes sukūn. It may also take kasra with the wāw, according to the original form.
Its lightening with the wāw is just like their lightening of "wa-hwa qāla dhāka" and "wa-hya qālat dhāka". The Banū Sulaym give the lām fatḥa when it begins the utterance and say "la-yaqum Zaydun", and they make the lām take fatḥa in every case, just as the Tamīm gave fatḥa to the lām of kay when they said: "jiʾtu la-ākhudha ḥaqqī" ("I came to take my due").
His saying: ﴿طَآئِفَةٌ أُخْرَىٰ﴾ — He did not say "ākharūn" (others, masc. pl.); then He said ﴿لَمْ يُصَلُّواْ﴾ and did not say "fal-tuṣalli" (feminine singular). Had it been said "fal-tuṣalli", just as "ukhrā" was said, it would have been permissible. And He said in another place: ﴿وإنْ طائفتانِ مِن المؤمِنِين اقتتلوا﴾; had "iqtatalatā" (dual feminine) been said in ordinary speech, it would have been correct.
Likewise His saying ﴿هذانِ خَصْمانِ اختصموا فى ربِّهم﴾, and He did not say "ikhtaṣamā" (dual). And He said ﴿فِرقا هدى وفرِيقا حَقَّ عليهم الضّلالة﴾; in the reading of Ubayy: "عليه الضلالة". So when you mention a masculine noun that denotes a group, it is permissible to make its verb plural or singular, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿وإنا لجميع حاذرون﴾ and His saying ﴿أم يقولون نَحْن جَميعٌ مُنْتَصر﴾. Likewise, if the noun is feminine and denotes a group — such as al-ṭāʾifa (party), al-ʿuṣba (band) and al-rufqa (company) — you make its verb like the verb of a single female; and if you wish, you make it plural and masculine according to the meaning. All of that has occurred in the Qurʾān.

farraa:104-104.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَرْجُونَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَرْجُونَ﴾ — one of the exegetes said: the meaning of «ترجون» is "you fear". But we have not found that hope (rajāʾ) carries the meaning of fear except when there is a negation with it. When that is the case, fear is in the sense of both hope and fear, and hope likewise; as in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿قل لِلذِين آمنوا يغفِروا لِلذِين لا يرجون أَيّامَ اللهِ﴾ — this means: those who do not fear the days of Allah. Likewise His saying: ﴿ما لكم لا تَرْجون لِلّهِ وقارا﴾: you do not fear the greatness of Allah. It is a Ḥijāzī usage. The rajaz poet said:
لا ترتجِى حِين تلاقى الذائدا * أسبعة لاقت معا أم واحدا
(She does not fear, when she meets the one who drives [camels] away from the water, whether she has met seven together or one.)
And al-Hudhalī said:
إذا لسعته النحلُ لم يرجَ لَسْعها * وخالفها فى بيتِ نُوب عوامِلِ
(When the bees sting him he does not fear their sting, and he comes upon them from behind in a home of busy working bees.)
It is not permissible to say "I hoped for you" when you mean "I feared you", nor "I feared you" when you mean "I hoped for you". [Translator's note: the text reads «الهدلى», evidently for «الهذلى» (al-Hudhalī).]

farraa:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَكْسِبْ خَطِيۤئَةً أَوْ إِثْماً ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئاً﴾ — it may be asked: how did He say "bihi" (with it, masculine singular) when He had mentioned both «الخطيئة» and «الإثم»?
That is permissible: two deeds, one of which is feminine, may be referred to with a masculine singular pronoun; and even if they were many, it would be permissible to refer to them with a singular, because a single action falls upon the [various] deeds; that is why it is permissible. If you wish, you combine «الخطيئة» and «الإثم» and treat them as one. And if you wish, you make the hāʾ refer to «الإثم» specifically; as He said ﴿وإذا رَأَوْا تجارةً أو لَهْواً انفَضُّوا إِليها﴾, making it [the pronoun] refer to trade. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (وإذا رأوا لهوا أو تجارة انفَضُّوا إليها), so he made it refer to trade whether it is placed first or last. Had the masculine been used, treating the two as one deed, it would have been permissible; and had the masculine been used with "amusement" in mind, it would have been permissible.
And He said ﴿إِن يكن غَنِيّاً أو فَقِيرا فاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بهما﴾, using the dual. So had the dual been used for "sin" and "amusement", "wrongdoing" and "trade", it would have been permissible. In the reading of Ubayy: (إن يكن غنِىّ أو فقير فالله أولى بهم), and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (إِن يكن غنىّ أو فقير فالله أولى بهما). As for Ubayy's (بهم), it is like His saying ﴿وكم مِن مَلَكٍ فى السمواتِ لا تُغْنِى شفاعَتُهمْ﴾: he had the plural in mind. That is how it came in Ubayy's reading, because He had mentioned them all together and then made "the rich" and "the poor" singular, while both are in the sense of a plural; just as you say: "The people became fasting and not fasting" (aṣbaḥa al-nāsu ṣāʾiman wa-mufṭiran), where two [singulars] convey the meaning of a plural.

farraa:113-113.t:
His saying: ﴿لَهَمَّتْ طَّآئِفَةٌ﴾ — He means "la-qad hammat ṭāʾifa" ("a party had certainly resolved"), and [«قد»] has been left implied.
His saying: ﴿أَن يُضِلُّوكَ﴾: to make you err in your judgement.

farraa:114-114.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّن نَّجْوَاهُمْ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ﴾ — (من) is in the position of the genitive or the accusative. The genitive: "except in the one who commands charity." "Al-najwā" here means men [who confer in secret], as He said ﴿وإذْ هُمْ نَجوى﴾. Whoever takes «النجوى» as an act [i.e. a verbal noun, "secret conference"], as He said ﴿ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثةٍ﴾, then (من) is in the position of the nominative. As for the accusative, it is when you take «النجوى» as an act [and the exception is from a different kind]. When you except something from what is different from it, the proper way is the accusative, as the poet said:
وقفت فيها أُصَيلاناً أُسائلها * عَيَّت جوابا وما بالربْعِ مِن أحدِ
إِلا الأوارِىَّ لأْياً ما أُبيِّنها * والنُؤْىُ كالحوض بالمظلومةِ الجَلَدِ
(I stood in it at late afternoon questioning it; it was unable to answer, and there was no one in the encampment — except the tethering-posts, which I can barely make out, and the trench, like a cistern, in the hard, untilled ground.)
It may also be in the position of the nominative even when it is referred back to what is different from it, as the poet said:
وبلد ليس بِهِ أنيسُ * إلا اليعافِيرُ وإلاَّ العِيسُ
(Many a land in which there is no companion, except the young gazelles and the whitish camels.)

farraa:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿إِن يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إِلاَّ إِنَاثاً﴾ — He is saying: al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā and the like among the female deities. Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿إِن يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إِلاَّ إِنَاثاً﴾ as the plural of wathan (idol): he gave the wāw a ḍamma and then turned it into a hamza, as He said ﴿وإذا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَت﴾. [Translator's note: the printed text repeats the standard wording «إناثا» here; the reading being described is «أُثُناً» (from wuthun, plural of wathan).] It has also been read (إنْ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِه إلا أُنُثا), the plural of «الإناث», so it is like thimār and thumur, as in ﴿كُلُوا مِنْ ثُمُرِه﴾.

farraa:118-118.t: His saying: ﴿نَصِيباً مَّفْرُوضاً﴾ — Allah gave him [Satan] a way over him [i.e. over that portion], so it is like something appointed.

farraa:119-119.t: His saying: ﴿وَلأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ﴾ — in the reading of Ubayy: "وأُضلهم وأُمَنِّيهم".

farraa:125-125.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلاً﴾ — someone may ask: what is this intimate friendship (khulla)? It is mentioned that Abraham ﷺ used to host guests and feed people. Then a year of drought struck the people and food became scarce. So Abraham ﷺ sent to a close friend (khalīl) of his in Egypt, from whom provisions used to come; he sent his servants with sacks and camels so that he might supply him with provisions. But [the friend] sent them back, saying: "Abraham does not want this for himself; he only wants it for others." He said: So his servants returned, and they passed by a valley of soft sand. They took some of its sand and filled the sacks, out of shame at bringing them back empty. They came back to Abraham ﷺ and told him the news while his wife was asleep; sleep overcame him out of worry. She woke up while the people were at the door seeking food. She said to the bakers: "Open these sacks and knead." They opened them, and there was the finest food. So they kneaded and baked. Abraham ﷺ woke up and smelt the food, and said: "Where is this from?" Abraham's ﷺ wife said: "This is from your Egyptian friend." He said: Abraham said: "This is from my Friend Allah, not from my Egyptian friend." He said: That is his intimate friendship (khulla).

farraa:127-127.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَىٰ﴾ (its meaning: Say, Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited). The position of (ما) is nominative, as though He said: "What is recited to you gives you a ruling concerning them." And if you wish, you can make «ما» be in the position of the genitive: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning what is recited to you other than them."
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾ is in the position of the genitive, on the basis of His saying: "He gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning the oppressed." His saying: ﴿وَأَن تَقُومُواْ﴾ — (أن) is in the position of the genitive, on the basis of His saying: "and He gives you a ruling concerning your standing firm for orphans with justice."

farraa:128-128.t:
His saying: ﴿خَافَتْ مِن بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزاً﴾ — nushūz (discord, ill-conduct) can come from the woman or the man. Here the nushūz is from the man, not the woman.
His nushūz is that he has an older wife and wants to marry a young woman in addition to her and to favour her in the division [of nights] and in intercourse. He should say to the older wife: "I want to marry a young woman in addition to you and to favour her over you." If she consents, that is acceptable for him; if she does not consent, she has the same share in the division as the young woman.
His saying: ﴿وَأُحْضِرَتِ ٱلأنْفُسُ ٱلشُّحَّ﴾ — by this He meant only the man and his older wife.
The man was stingy with his share of the young woman, and the older woman was stingy with her share of him. Then He said: and if she is content with the arrangement (al-imra). [Translator's note: «بالإمرة» is as printed; the sense appears to be "with this arrangement / with his decision".]

farraa:129-129.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَمِيلُواْ كُلَّ ٱلْمَيْلِ﴾ — toward the young woman, so that you abandon the older one entirely ﴿فَتَذَرُوهَا كَٱلْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾. In the reading of Ubayy it is (كالمسجونة) ("like one imprisoned").

farraa:135-135.t:
His saying: ﴿كُونُواْ قَوَّامِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ شُهَدَآءِ للَّهِ﴾ — this concerns giving testimony against themselves and against parents and relatives. And do not look at the wealth of the rich or the poverty of the poor, for Allah is more entitled to that.
(فلا تَتَّبِعُوا الهوى [أن تعدِلوا]) — in flight from giving testimony. It may also be said: "Do not follow desire, so that you may be just," just as you say: "Do not follow your desire, so that you may please your Lord," i.e. I forbid you this so that you may please your Lord.
His saying ﴿وَإِن تَلْوُواْ﴾ — and «تَلُوا» — both have been read. We think that those who said (تلوا) meant «تَلْؤُوا»: they turned the wāw into a hamza because of its ḍamma, then dropped the hamza, so that the vowel of the hamza moved to the lām and the hamza fell away. Unless the meaning in it is: "and if you take charge (talū) of that," meaning "you undertake it", ﴿أَوْ تُعْرِضُواْ﴾ from it, i.e. or you abandon it — that is a [valid] interpretation.

farraa:137-137.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ثُمَّ كَفَرُواْ ثُمَّ آمَنُواْ ثُمَّ كَفَرُواْ﴾ — these are those who believed in Moses and then disbelieved after him by [what they said about] ʿUzayr, then believed in ʿUzayr and disbelieved in Jesus. And the Jews believed in Moses and disbelieved in Jesus.
Then He said: ﴿[ثُمَّ] ٱزْدَادُواْ كُفْراً﴾ — He means the Jews: they increased in unbelief by their disbelieving in Muhammad ﷺ.

farraa:90-90.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِّيثَاقٌ﴾ — He is saying: when a people made a covenant with the Prophet ﷺ that they would not fight him nor help [others] against him, and wrote a peace treaty, it was not lawful to fight them, nor anyone who joined himself to them, for his position on fighting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the same as theirs, and so it was not lawful to fight him. That is His saying (يصلون), meaning: they join themselves to them.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ جَآءُوكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ﴾ — He is saying: their breasts are constricted from fighting you or fighting their own people. That is the meaning of His saying ﴿حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ﴾, i.e. their breasts are constricted.
Al-Ḥasan read "حصِرةً صدورهم" [as a ḥāl (circumstantial)]. The Arabs say: "atānī dhahaba ʿaqluhu" ("he came to me, his mind gone"), meaning "qad dhahaba ʿaqluhu". Al-Kisāʾī heard one of them say: "fa-aṣbaḥtu naẓartu ilā dhāti al-tanānīr" ("and in the morning I had looked toward Dhāt al-Tanānīr"). So whenever you see faʿala [a past verb] after kāna, «قد» is implied in it — unless there is a negation (jaḥd) with kāna, in which case «قد» is not implied with the negation, because it is for emphasis and a negation is not emphasised [in this way]. Do you not see that you say "mā dhahabtu" ("I did not go"), but "mā qad dhahabtu" is not permissible?

farraa:91-91.t: His saying: ﴿سَتَجِدُونَ آخَرِينَ يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَأْمَنُوكُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: that they may be safe among you and safe among their own people. These are in the same position as those we have mentioned, in that fighting them is lawful if they do not turn back.

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ﴾ — it is in the nominative according to your saying: "then upon him is the freeing of a slave." The "believing" one is one who prays and has reached the age of discernment. If He had not said "a believing slave", a small child who neither prays nor has come of age would suffice.
His saying: ﴿فَإِن كَانَ مِن قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَّكُمْ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ — a man would become Muslim among his own people while they were unbelievers, and he would conceal his Islam. Whoever of these was killed while his Islam was not known, his killer would free a slave, and his blood-money was not paid to the unbelievers, lest they be strengthened by it against the people of Islam. That is when there was no treaty between his people and the Prophet ﷺ; if there was a treaty, he was treated like [any other] Muslim.

farraa:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ إِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُواْ﴾ — (فَتَثَبَّتُوا is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and his companions; likewise the one in [Sūrat] al-Ḥujurāt. And the two are read: فَتَثَبَّتُوا.) [Translator's note: the parenthesis is as in the printed text; its last clause appears to repeat فتثبتوا where فتبينوا may have been intended.] The two are close in meaning. You say to a man: "Do not hasten to act until you have made it clear and made sure."
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُواْ لِمَنْ أَلْقَىۤ إِلَيْكُمُ ٱلسَّلاَمَ لَسْتَ مُؤْمِناً﴾ — they mention that it was a man who greeted one of the Muslim raiding parties with "peace", and they thought that he was taking refuge in Islam and was not [really] a Muslim, and he was killed. The generality read it: «السَلَم». Al-salam is surrender and giving oneself up.

farraa:95-95.t: His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَسْتَوِي ٱلْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ غَيْرُ أُوْلِي ٱلضَّرَرِ﴾ — (غير) is put in the nominative so that it is like a naʿt (adjective) for «القاعدين», as He said: ﴿صِراطَ الذين أنعمت عليهم غيرِ المغضوب﴾, and as He said ﴿أوِ التابِعِين غيرِ أولِى الإرْبةِ مِن الرجالِ﴾. It has been mentioned that (غير) was revealed after the superiority of the one who strives over the one who stays behind had been mentioned, so the proper way would have been exception (istithnāʾ) and the accusative. However, the close joining of (غير) to «القاعدين» all but requires the nominative, because exception should come after the [clause is] complete. Thus you say in speech: "The doers of good and the doers of evil are not equal, except so-and-so and so-and-so." It may also be in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as He said: ﴿أُحِلَّتْ لكم بهيمةُ الأنعامِ إلا ما يُتْلَى عليكم غيرَ مُحِلِّى الصيدِ﴾. If it were read in the genitive, that would be a valid way: you would make it a description of «المؤمنين».

farraa:97-97.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾ — if you wish, you can treat ﴿تَوَفَّاهُمُ﴾ as being in the position of the accusative [i.e. a past verb, tawaffāhum], without implying a second tāʾ alongside the tāʾ; it is then like His saying ﴿إن البقر تشابه علينا﴾. And if you wish, you can treat it as nominative [i.e. an imperfect verb], meaning: "Those whom the angels take (tatawaffāhum)." In every place where two tāʾs come together, it is permissible to drop one of them, as in His saying ﴿لعلكم تذكرون﴾ and His saying ﴿فإن تَوَلَّوْا فقد أبلغتكم﴾.

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾ — it is in the position of the accusative as an exception from ﴿مأواهم جهنم﴾.

farraa:141-141.t: His saying: ﴿أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ عَلَيْكُمْ وَنَمْنَعْكُمْ﴾ — it is jussive. [It would also be possible] if you put it in the accusative by interpretation as ṣarf [the wāw of concomitance], as in your saying in speech: "Did we not gain mastery over you, when we had already protected you?" It would then be like His saying ﴿ولمّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِين جاهَدوا مِنْكم ويَعْلَمَ الصابرين﴾. In the reading of Ubayy it is (ومنعناكم من المؤمنين). If you wish, you can take "wa-manaʿnākum" in the sense of "wa-qad kunnā manaʿnākum" ("and we had protected you"); and if you wish, you can take it as referred back to the sense of ﴿أَلَمْ﴾, as though He said: "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you?" In the reading of Ubayy [similarly]: (أَلَمْ تُنْهيَا عن تِلْكُما الشّجَرَةِ وقِيلَ لكما).

farraa:145-145.t: His saying: ﴿فِي ٱلدَّرْكِ ٱلأَسْفَلِ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾ — one says al-dark and al-darak, i.e. the lowest level in the Fire.

farraa:146-146.t: His saying: ﴿فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مَعَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis: (من المؤمنين) ("[are] of the believers").

farraa:148-148.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ يُحِبُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْجَهْرَ بِٱلسُّوۤءِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ﴾ — and [also read] «ظَلَمَ». (مَنْ) may in both readings be accusative as an exception disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) from the first [part]. And if you wish, you can make (من) nominative when you read (ظُلم), the meaning then being: "Allah does not love that anyone should speak evil openly, except the one who has been wronged." That is the guest: when he wants to lodge with a man and he refuses him, he has wronged him, and he is permitted to mention him for what he did, because he denied him his due.
Or ﴿لاَّ يُحِبُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْجَهْرَ بِٱلسُّوۤءِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ﴾ may be a complete statement, after which He says: "except the wrongdoer, so leave him be." It is then like the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, ﴿لئلاّ يكونَ لِلناسِ عليكم حُجّة إِلا الِذين ظَلَموا﴾, for the wrongdoer has no argument; it is as though He said: "except whoever does wrong — leave him alone." It is like His saying ﴿فذكِّر إنما أنت مُذَكِّر﴾, then He made an exception and said ﴿إِلا مَنْ تَوَلَّى وكفر﴾: the exception is from His saying ﴿إنما أنت مُذَكّر﴾, although there are no nouns in it, and the exception is not from His saying ﴿لَسْتَ عَلَيْهم بمصيطر﴾. Similar to it, among cases where it is permissible to except nouns when no overt [noun] precedes them, is your saying: "I hate quarrelling and disputation — O Allah, except a man who intends Allah by it." Excepting "a man" is permissible although no noun was mentioned before it, because quarrelling and disputation take place only between human beings. [Translator's note: «جعت» in the text is evidently a misprint for «جعلت».]

farraa:155-155.t: His saying: ﴿قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ﴾ — i.e. [our hearts are] vessels for knowledge, which they know and understand; so why is it that we do not understand what (Muhammad ﷺ) brings? So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿بَلْ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.

farraa:157-157.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ﴾ — the hāʾ here refers to Jesus ﷺ.
His saying ﴿وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِيناً﴾ — the hāʾ here refers to knowledge, as you say "I killed it in knowledge" and "I killed it in certainty" [i.e. I mastered it thoroughly], of an opinion, a report or a supposition.

farraa:159-159.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ إِلاَّ لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾ — its meaning is: [there is none of them except one] who will surely believe in him before his death. The exegesis has come in two ways. One of them is that the hāʾ in «موته» refers to Jesus: He is saying, they will believe when he descends, before his death, and the religion and creed will be one.
It is also said: every Jew will believe in Jesus at his [own] death. What confirms that is the reading of Ubayy: (إلا ليؤمنُنَّ به قبل موتهم) ("before their death").

farraa:163-163.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ كَمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ﴾ — as We revealed to all of them.

farraa:164-164.t:
His saying: ﴿وَرُسُلاً قَدْ قَصَصْنَاهُمْ عَلَيْكَ﴾ — its accusative can be explained in two ways. It may come from your saying: "as We revealed to messengers before you"; when you drop «إلى», and [the sense of] sending, it attaches to the verb and becomes accusative, as in His saying ﴿يُدْخِل من يشاء فِى رحمتِهِ والظالِمين أَعدّ لهم عذابا أَليما﴾. Or it may be accusative by (قصصناهم) [an implied verb explained by it].
Had it been nominative, it would have been correct, because of the pronoun that refers back to them. In the reading of Ubayy it is nominative: (ورُسُلٌ قَدْ قَصَصْناهم عليك من قَبْل ورسلٌ لم نَقْصُصْهُمْ عليك).

farraa:170-170.t: His saying: ﴿فَآمِنُواْ خَيْراً لَّكُمْ﴾ — (خير) is accusative by its connection with the command, because it is a description of the command. This can be shown: do you not see that a pronoun referring to the command can stand before «خير», so that you say to a man: "Fear Allah, it is better for you," i.e. fearing [Allah] is better for you? When (هو) drops, it attaches to what precedes it, which is definite, and becomes accusative. Its accusative is not by implying (يكن) ("it will be"), because that would lead to an analogy that invalidates this. Do you not see that you say "Fear Allah, you will be (takun) a doer of good," but it is not permissible to say "Fear Allah, a doer of good (muḥsinan)" while implying (تكن); nor is it right to say "Help us, our brother (akhānā)" (meaning "you will be our brother").

farraa:171-171.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُواْ ثَلاَثَةٌ﴾ — i.e. [do not] say: "They are three"; as in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿سيقولون ثلاثَةٌ رابعهم﴾. Whenever you see [a noun] in the nominative after "saying" with nothing to make it nominative, there is an implied noun in it that makes that noun nominative [i.e. an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject)].
His saying: ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ﴾ — «من» or «عن» is fit [to be supplied] before (أن); when they are dropped, (أن) is in the position of the accusative. Al-Kisāʾī used to say: it is in the position of the genitive, in many of its like.

farraa:173-173.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَجِدُونَ﴾ — it is referred back to what comes after the fāʾ, and so is nominative. Had it been jussive, referring back to the position of the fāʾ, it would have been correct, as He said ﴿من يضلِلِ الله فلا هادِى له ويذرهم﴾.

farraa:176-176.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن ٱمْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ﴾ — (هلك) is in the position of the jussive. Likewise His saying ﴿وإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ اسْتَجَارَكَ﴾: had there been a yafʿalu-verb in their place, both would have been jussive; as al-Kumayt said:
فإن أنت تفعل فللفاعلين * أنت المجيزين تلك الغمارا
(If you do [it], then [it is fitting] for the doers — you [being one of] those who cross those floods.)
And one of them recited:
صعدة نابتة فى حائِرٍ * أَينما الريح تُمَيِّلْها تمِل
(A straight reed growing in a pool: wherever the wind bends it, it bends.)
However, when the verb comes after the noun in a conditional (jazāʾ), the Arabs prefer to make it faʿala [a past verb], because the jussive is not visible in faʿala, and they dislike that anything should intervene between the word that governs the jussive and what it puts in the jussive.
His saying ﴿يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَن تَضِلُّواْ﴾ — its meaning is: "lest you go astray (allā taḍillū)." That is why «لا» is fit in the place of «أن». This is a test for (أن): when «لئلا» and «كيلا» are fit in its place, «لا» is fit.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾: He said (واحدة) because النفس is feminine; He said واحدة for the femininity of النفس, and it [means] Ādam. Had it been (من نفس واحد), it would have been correct, going by the masculinity of the man.
And His saying: ﴿وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا﴾: the Arabs say: بثَّ الله الخلق, i.e. He spread them out. And He said in another place: ﴿كالفَراشِ المَبْثوث﴾. Some of the Arabs say: أَبثّ الله الخلق.
They also say: بثثتك ما فى نفسى and أبثثتك ("I disclosed to you what was in my heart").
And His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِي تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِ وَٱلأَرْحَامَ﴾: He put الأرحام in the accusative, meaning: and fear [to sever] the wombs [i.e. ties of kinship] — lest you sever them. He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me from al-Aʿmash from Ibrāhīm that he read الأرحام in the genitive; he said: it is like their saying: بالله والرحم ("by Allah and by kinship"). There is ugliness in this, because the Arabs do not coordinate a genitive noun onto a genitive that has been expressed by a pronoun. The poet did say, permitting it:
نُعَلّق فى مثلِ السَّوارِى سيوفَنا * وما بينها والْكَعبِ غَوْط نَفَانِف
(We hang our swords on [necks] like pillars, and between them and the heel is a deep, sheer drop.)
But this is permissible only in poetry, because of its constraint.
And some read "تَسَّاءلون به", meaning تتساءلون به; the tāʾ was assimilated into the sīn.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَبَدَّلُواْ ٱلْخَبِيثَ بِٱلطَّيِّبِ﴾: He is saying: do not consume the wealth of orphans in place of your own wealth, when their wealth is forbidden to you and your own wealth is lawful.
And His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ حُوباً كَبِيراً﴾: الحوب is the great sin. I have seen Banū Asad say الحائب for the killer; and حاب يحوب ("he sinned"). Al-Ḥasan read (إنه كان حَوْبا كبيرا). «[Translator's note: the source has العظم, presumably a misprint for العظيم "great".]»

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تُقْسِطُواْ فِي ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ﴾: the orphans in this place are those possessing wealth. Someone may ask: what turned the speech from the wealth of orphans to marriage? It is said: they had abandoned mixing with orphans out of scruple, so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed: if you feel scruples about eating together with orphans, then feel scruples about combining women and then not being just among them; ﴿فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ﴾, meaning from one to four.
The Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ﴾ and did not say: من طاب. That is because He went by the act [i.e. the sense of a maṣdar], as He said ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾, meaning: or what your right hands possess. Had (من) been said in these two, it would have been correct, but the best way is what the Book brought. You say in ordinary speech: خذ من عبيدى ما شئت ("take of my slaves what you wish"), when he means your wish; and if you say: من شئت, its meaning is: take whomever you wish.
As for His saying: ﴿مَثْنَىٰ وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾, these are words that are not declined fully (lā tujrā, diptotes). That is because they are diverted from their [original] forms; do you not see that they stand for ثلاث and ثلاثة, and that they are not annexed to what ثلاثة and ثلاث are annexed to? So, owing to its refusal of annexation, it is as if it had the alif and lām in it.
And it refuses the alif and lām because there is a sense of annexation in it; just as the structure of ثلاثة is to be annexed to its kind, so that it is said: ثلاث نسوة ("three women") and ثلاثة رجال ("three men").
Sometimes they put in place of ثُلاَث and رُبَاع the forms مَثْلَث and مَرْبَع, and these too are not declined fully, just as ثُلاث and رُباع are not, because it is diverted, and has the same cause as ثُلاث and رُباع. Whoever makes them indefinite and takes them as nouns declines them fully.
The Arabs say: ادخلوا ثُلاثَ ثُلاثَ and ثُلاثا ثلاثا ("enter three by three"). The poet said:
[وإنَّ الغلام المستهام بذكره] * قتَلْنا به مِن بَين مَثْنىً ومَوْحدِ
بأربعةٍ منكم وآخر خامسٍ * وسادٍ مع الإظلام فى رمح معبدِ
([And the youth, infatuated with his memory —] for him we killed, in twos and ones, four of you and another, a fifth, and a sixth at nightfall on the spear of Maʿbad.)
So the proper way of the speech is that they not be declined fully and be treated as definite, because they are diverted, and the nature of a diverted form is to be left as it is, like لُكَع and لَكاع. Likewise His saying: ﴿أُولِى أَجنِحةٍ مَثْنَى وثُلاثَ ورُباع﴾.
For one, it is said مَوْحَد, أُحاد and وُحاد; and مثنى and ثُنَاء. One of them recited:
تَرى النُّعَراتِ الزُّرْقَ تحتَ لَبانه * أُحادَ ومَثْنَى أَصْعَقَتْها صَواهله
(You see the blue horseflies beneath his chest, in ones and twos, struck senseless by his neighing.)
And His saying: ﴿فَوَاحِدَةً﴾ is accusative on [the sense]: if you fear that you will not be just among the four in love and intercourse, then marry one, or what your right hands possess, in which no fixed number is imposed on you. Had He said فواحدةٌ, in the nominative, it would be as He said ﴿فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان﴾; it would be correct, in the sense of your saying: فواحدة (suffices — فواحدة) is acceptable.
And His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰ أَلاَّ تَعُولُواْ﴾: that you do not incline [to injustice]. It is also in the speech of the Arabs: قد عال يعول. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ولا يَعُلْ أن يأتِينِى بهم جميعا), as if in meaning: and let it not be burdensome for him to bring them all to me. Of poverty one says: عال يعيل عَيْلة; and the poet said:
ولا يدرى الفقير متى غناه * ولا يدرى الغنِىُّ متى يَعِيل
(The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, nor does the rich man know when he will become poor.)
«[Translator's note: the source prints the second يدرى as يردى, a misprint.]»

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً﴾ means the guardians of the women, not the husbands. That is because in the Jāhiliyya they used not to give women anything of their dowers, so Allah the Exalted revealed: give them their dowers as نحلة, He is saying: as a gift and a present.
And His saying: ﴿فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَيْءٍ مِّنْهُ نَفْساً﴾: He did not say طبن [only]. That is because the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: if their souls are pleased to give you something of it. So the verb was transferred from the souls to them, and النفس came out as an explicative (tamyīz (specification)); as they say: أنت حسن وجها ("you are handsome of face"), where the act originally belongs to the face; when it was transferred to the owner of the face, the face came out as an explicative of the place of the act. For that reason النفس is singular; had it been plural, it would have been correct. Similar to it is ضاق به ذراعى ("my arm was straitened by it"); then the verb is transferred from the arm to you; and you say: قَرِرت به عينا ("I was cooled of eye by it", i.e. delighted). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿فكلِى واشربى وقرّى عينا﴾, and He said: ﴿سِىء بِهِم وضاق بهم ذرعا﴾; and the poet said:
إذا التّيَّازُ ذو العَضلات قلنا * إليك إليك ضاق بها ذراعا
(When we say to the brawny, muscular man, "Take it! Take it!", he is straitened by it in arm.)
It was said ذرعا and ذراعا only because the maṣdar and the noun in this place indicate one meaning; therefore the maṣdar sufficed in place of the noun.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُؤْتُواْ ٱلسُّفَهَآءَ أَمْوَالَكُمُ﴾: the foolish are women and children. ﴿ٱلَّتِي جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ قِيَاماً﴾: He is saying: [the wealth] by which you subsist — قواما and قياما. Nāfiʿ of Medina read (قِيَما), and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is the same.
The Arabs say (اللاتى) for the plural of women more than they say (التى), and they say (التى) for the plural of wealth and all things other than women more than they say (اللاتى).

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِّنْهُمْ رُشْداً﴾ means: if you find. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "فإن أحَسْتم منهم رشدا".
﴿فَٱدْفَعُواْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ refers to the guardians and the orphans.
And His saying: ﴿وَبِدَاراً أَن يَكْبَرُواْ﴾: (أن) is in the position of the accusative. He is saying: do not hasten [to consume it] ahead of their growing up.
And His saying: ﴿فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾: this is the guardian. He is saying: he eats as a loan.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصيِبٌ﴾, then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿نَصِيباً مَّفْرُوضاً﴾. He put the "appointed share" in the accusative, though it qualifies an indefinite, only because He treated it as a maṣdar. Had it been a proper noun, it would not be accusative. Rather it is like your saying: لك علىّ حقّ حقّا ("you have a right against me, truly"), whereas you do not say: لك على حقّ درهما. Similar is عندى درهمان هبةً مقبوضة ("I have two dirhams as a gift received"). So المفروض in this place is like your saying: فريضة and فرضا ("as an obligation").

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يُورَثُ كَلاَلَةً﴾: الكلالة is [heirs] other than child and parent.
And His saying: ﴿وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ﴾, and He did not say: ولهما. This is permissible: when two words come with أو in a single sense, you attach the explanation [the pronoun] to whichever of them you wish; and if you wish, you mention them both in it. You say in ordinary speech: من كان له أخ أو أخت فليصِلْه ("whoever has a brother or sister, let him keep ties with him"), going by the brother, (and) فليصِلها, going by the sister. And if you say (فليصلهما), that is permissible.
In our reading it is (إن يكن غنِيا أو فقِيرا فالله أولى بِهِما), and in one of the two readings (فالله أولى بهم), going by the plural because they are two non-specific [persons]. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (والذين يفعلون مِنكم فآذوهما), going by the plural because they are two non-specific [persons]; likewise in his reading: (والسارقون والسارقات فاقطعوا أيمانهما).
And His saying: ﴿غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّ﴾: He is saying: he makes that bequest without causing harm.
And the accusative of His word وصية in His saying: ﴿لِكلّ واحِدٍ منهما السُّدسُ - وصِيةً مِن الله﴾ is like your saying: لك درهمان نفقةً إلى أهلك ("you have two dirhams as maintenance for your family"); and it is like His saying ﴿نصيبا مفروضا﴾.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ﴾ means: these are the limits of Allah.

farraa:15-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱللاَّتِي يَأْتِينَ ٱلْفَاحِشَةَ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (واللاتى يأتِين بالفاحشة). The Arabs say: أتيت أمرا عظيما and أتيت بأمر عظيم ("I committed a grave thing"), تكلمت كلاما قبيحا and بكلام قبيح ("I spoke ugly words"). He said in Maryam ﴿لقد جِئتِ شيئا فرِيّا﴾ and ﴿جِئتم شيئا إِدّا﴾; had the bāʾ been in it, it would have been correct.
And His saying: ﴿فأمسِكوهن فِى البيوتِ﴾: they used to be confined in houses of their own when they committed indecency, until Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّذَانَ يَأْتِيَانِهَا مِنكُمْ فَآذُوهُمَا﴾, and this abrogated the first. «[Translator's note: the source has فنسحت, a misprint for فنسخت "abrogated".]»

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿ ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِن قَرِيبٍ﴾: He is saying: before death. Whoever repents in his health or in his illness before death descends upon him, his repentance is accepted. And His saying: ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسُّوۤءَ بِجَهَالَةٍ﴾: they are not ignorant that it is a sin, but they do not know the full reality of what is in it as the learned man knows it.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ﴾: (الذين) is in the position of the genitive. He is saying: if the unbeliever embraces Islam in his illness before death descends upon him, it is accepted; but when death has descended upon him, there is no repentance.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرْهاً﴾: when a man died leaving his wife, and he had a son by another woman, the son would leap up and throw his garment over her, and marry her with no dower except the first one's dower; then he would harm her so as to inherit from her what she had inherited from his father. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed: ﴿لاَ يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرْهاً وَلاَ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ﴾. (تعضلوهن) is in the position of the accusative by أن. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (ولا أن تعضلوهنّ). Had it been jussive as a prohibition, it would have been correct.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَدْ أَفْضَىٰ بَعْضُكُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾: الإفضاء is that he is alone with her in private, even if he has not had intercourse with her.
And His saying ﴿مِّيثَاقاً غَلِيظاً﴾: the firm [covenant] that they [the wives] took is His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فإمساك بِمعروفٍ أو تسريحٌ بإحسان﴾. «[Translator's note: the source reads الغليظ الذى أخذنه قوله, which is awkward; it is translated according to its evident sense.]»

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَن تَجْمَعُواْ بَيْنَ ٱلاخْتَيْنِ﴾: أن is in the position of the nominative, as if you said: والجمع بين الأختين ("and combining two sisters").

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾: المحصنات are the chaste women; and المحصنات are also the married women, whom their husbands have made muḥṣan (protected).
The fatḥa in المحصنات is more common. ʿAlqama related "المحصِنات" with kasra throughout the Qurʾān except for His saying ﴿والمحصَنات من النّساء﴾, this one word, because she is the married woman among the captives of the polytheists. He is saying: if she has a husband in her own land, you ascertain her freedom from pregnancy by one menstrual period, and she becomes lawful for you.
And His saying ﴿كِتابَ اللَّه عليكم﴾ is like your saying: كتابا من الله عليكم ("as a prescription from Allah upon you"). Some of the grammarians said: its meaning is: عليكم كتاب الله ("hold to the Book of Allah"). The first is closer to correct. The Arabs seldom say: زيدا عليك or زيدا دونك [putting the noun before the verbal noun]; it is permissible, as if it were accusative by something implied before it. The poet said:
يأيُّها المائحُ دَلْوى دونكا * إنى رأيت الناس يَحْمَدُونكا
(O you who fill the buckets at the bottom of the well, here is my bucket; I have seen people praising you.)
الدلو is nominative, as when you say: زيد فاضربوه ("Zayd — strike him"). The Arabs say: الليلُ فبادروا and الليلَ فبادروا ("the night — hasten [before it]"). And you may put الدلو in the accusative by something implied in the omission, as if you said: دونك دلوى دونك.
And His saying: ﴿وَأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ مَّا وَرَاءَ ذَلِكُمْ﴾: He is saying: what is other than that.
And His saying: ﴿وَيَكْفُرون بما وَراءَه﴾ means: what is other than it.
And His saying: ﴿أن تَبْتَغُوا﴾: its position may be nominative, as an explanation of (ما); and if you wish it may be genitive, meaning: Allah has made lawful for you what is beyond that, so that you may seek. And when the genitive particle is missing, it is accusative.
And His saying: ﴿مُّحْصِنِينَ﴾: He is saying: that you seek the lawful, not fornication. المسافحة is fornication.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ ٱلْعَنَتَ مِنْكُمْ﴾: He is saying: you are permitted to marry slave-women only when one of you fears that he will commit immorality. Then He said: but for you to refrain from marrying them is better.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ﴾, and He said in another place ﴿والله يُرِيدُ أن يتوبَ عليكم﴾: the Arabs put the lām that has the sense of كى in the place of أن with أردت and أمرت. So you say: أردت أن تذهب and أردت لتذهب ("I wanted you to go"), أمرتك أن تقوم and أمرتك لتقوم ("I commanded you to stand"). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿وأُمِرنا لِنُسْلِم لِربِّ العَالمِين﴾, and He said in another place ﴿قل إِنى أُمِرت أن أكون أوّل من أسلم﴾; and He said ﴿يرِيدون لِيطفِئوا﴾ and ﴿أن يطفِئوا﴾. The lām is suitable in the place of أن with (أمرتك) and أردت only because both of these call for the future and are not suitable with the past; do you not see that you say: أمرتك أن تقوم, but أمرتك أن قمت is not acceptable? So when they saw that (أن) with verbs other than these two can be for past and future, they made sure of the future sense with كى and with the lām that has the sense of كى. Sometimes they combine all three; Abū Tharwān recited to me:
أردت لكيما لا ترى لىَ عَثْرَةً * ومَنْ ذا الذى يُعْطَى الكمالَ فيَكْملُ
(You wished that you would never see a slip from me — but who is it that is given perfection and is perfect?)
So he combined (the lām and كى). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿لِكيلا تَأْسَوْا على ما فاتكم﴾. And another said, combining them:
أردتَ لكيما أن تَطَير بِقرْبتى * فتتركهَا شَنّا ببيداءَ بلقع
(You wanted to fly off with my water-skin and leave it a dried-out old skin in an empty desert.)
They combined them only because they agree in meaning and differ in form; as Ruʾba said:
* بِغيرِ لا عَصْفٍ ولا اصْطِرافِ *
(Without any earning or striving for gain.)
And sometimes they combine ما, لا and the إن that has the sense of negation; al-Kisāʾī recited to me in one of the verses: (لا ما إن رأيت مثلك) ("never, never have I seen your like"), combining three particles.
Sometimes the Arabs put the lām in place of (أن) with verbs resembling (أردت and أمرت), which call for the future. Al-Anfī, of Banū Anf al-Nāqa of Banū Saʿd, recited to me:
ألم تسأَلِ الأنفىَّ يومَ يَسُوقنى * ويَزْعم أنى مُبْطِلُ القولِ كاذِبُهْ
أحاولَ إعناتى بما قال أم رجا * ليضحك منى أو ليضْحك صاحبُهْ
(Did you not ask al-Anfī, the day he drove me on, claiming that my speech was vain and false: did he try to distress me by what he said, or did he hope to laugh at me, or that his companion might laugh?)
The [normal] speech is: رجا أن يضحك منى. But it is not permissible to say: ظننت لتقوم. That is because the (أن) that goes with supposing occurs with the past of the verb, so you say: أظنّ (أن قد) قام زيد ("I think Zayd has stood up"); and with the future, so you say: أظنّ أن سيقوم زيد ("I think Zayd will stand"); and with nouns, so you say: أظنّ أنك قائم ("I think you are standing"). So neither the lām nor كى was put in its place, since it does not call for the future alone.
Whenever you see that (أن) is suitable with both the future and the past, do not bring كى or the lām in upon it.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ نَاراً﴾ is also read نَصْلِيه. They are two dialect forms, and both have been read, from صَلَيْتُ and أَصليت. It is as if صَلَيْت means: you roast him on the fire; and أصليت: you make him enter it.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنُدْخِلْكُمْ مُّدْخَلاً كَرِيماً﴾ — and مَدخلا; likewise ﴿أَدْخلنى مَُدْخَل صدق وأخرجنى مَُخْرَج صدق﴾, [in the sense of] إدخال صدق ("a true entering-in"). Whoever says مَدخلا, مَخرجا and مَنزلا, it is as if he built it on: أدخلنى دخول صدق وأخرجنى خروج صدق ("cause me to enter a true entry and exit a true exit"). When it has fatḥa it may also be meant as the place itself, as He said: ﴿ربّ أنزلنى مَنزِلا مباركا﴾; and had you given the mīm fatḥa, it would be like "the house" and "the dwelling". «[Translator's note: the context suggests "had you given the mīm ḍamma" is intended in the second clause; the source reads فتحت (fatḥa) in both places.]» Sometimes the Arabs give fatḥa to the mīm of it, while the verb of it is only said as afʿaltu. Of that is his saying:
* بمَصْبح الحمد وحيث يُمسى *
(At the morning-time of praise, and wherever he passes the evening.)
And another said:
الحمد لله ممسانا ومَُصْبَحنا * بالخير صبّحنا ربى ومسَّانا
(Praise be to Allah at our evening and our morning; my Lord has brought us morning and evening with good.)
And al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
واعددت للحرب وثّابة * جواد المحثّة والمَرْود
(And I have prepared for war a leaping [mare], swift when urged and when let go at ease.)
This is something not built on faʿaltu, but only on arwadtu. Since the wāw appears in المُرود, it also appears in المَرود, just as they said مَصْبح while its base is only أصبحت.
